title: The --ivault flag: devbin resolves the Intent vault references in a command's environment before it runs the command
objective: With --ivault, devbin has Intent resolve each intent:// reference that the command's environment holds, before the command runs. hv schedules this package, and it does not start before hv says start.
body:
## Not before hv's word

hv schedules this package: it does not start before hv says start (vc hold 2). Its trigger is also upstream: stage 0 of the build of Intent's ST0060, with that thread's AC-00.19 (every terminal path resolves, or the flag is refused outright, with no partial). Intent's vc says when that design has stopped moving. No design or spike is made before then.

## What it does

--ivault is a global devbin flag. Before devbin runs a command, it resolves in place, through Intent, each intent:// reference that the process's environment already holds. It never reads a vault entry's key_id.

## The constraints

1. devbin never parses an intent:// reference. It tests for the literal prefix alone, and Intent makes the one parse. The literal test can over-trigger, at the cost of one process, and it cannot under-trigger.
2. Every terminal path of a command resolves, or the flag is refused outright. No path runs half-resolved.
3. The seam is in lib/resolve. exec_handler execs a project's or devbin's handler. _run_line runs every config or catalogue command line, bare by exec, or sealed through run_gate. A sealed run returns so that its seal is written, so it cannot be wrapped in an exec.
4. A dispatch change reaches every project that vendors devbin, so it ships as a release and a sweep, not as one commit.

## Open

Its spelling and its messages are set when Intent's design stops moving, and its size, M, is a first estimate until then. Its shape is devbin-ic's word, and its build is hv's call.
